canonicalExplanation.summary: A link's `href` can be **absolute** (`https://example.com/a`), **root-relative** (`/courses/css/`, from the site root), **relative** (`../css/`, from the **current page's folder**), or a **fragment** (`#forms`, a spot on the same page). Relative URLs resolve from the page they're written on — so moving a page can break them.

sections.heading: Start here
sections.body:
Your course site has `/courses/html/index.html` and `/courses/css/index.html`. A link to the CSS course works on one page but 404s on another. The link didn't change — the page it's on did. From /courses/html/index.html, the relative link ../css/ resolves to /courses/css/ under the current base. In this lesson you'll construct and debug links across a multi-folder site and within a page.

```predict
{"question": "On `/courses/html/index.html`, where does `href=\"forms.html\"` go?", "options": ["/forms.html", "/courses/html/forms.html"], "answer": 1, "why": "A plain relative URL resolves from the current page's folder: /courses/html/."}
```

sections.heading: Before you begin
sections.body: You should know **Sections and landmarks**, **Files, folders and paths** (relative paths and `..`), and the **Standards-mode document skeleton**.

sections.heading: The model: resolve from the current page's folder
sections.body:
```text
site root /
└── courses/
    ├── html/index.html     ← you are here
    └── css/index.html
```

| href on /courses/html/index.html | Resolves to |
|---|---|
| `forms.html` | /courses/html/forms.html. |
| `../css/` | /courses/css/. |
| `/courses/css/` | /courses/css/ (from the root). |
| `https://mdn.dev/` | that exact site. |
| `#forms` | the element with id="forms" on this page. |

```reveal
{"prompt": "What does `../css/` mean step by step?", "answer": "Start in /courses/html/, `..` goes up to /courses/, then `css/` enters the css folder → /courses/css/ (which serves its index.html)."}
```

examples.title: From the HTML course to the CSS course
examples.situation: From /courses/html/index.html, the relative link ../css/ resolves to /courses/css/ under the current base.
walkthrough: **Current base:** the page lives at /courses/html/index.html, so its folder is /courses/html/.
**Resolve ../css/:** `..` moves up to /courses/, then `css/` enters the css folder.
**Result:** the browser will navigate to /courses/css/, and that folder's index.html loads.
examples.result: The link reaches the CSS course from the HTML course page.

examples.title: The link that broke after moving a page
examples.situation: `about.html` at the root links to `img/team.jpg`. The page is moved to `/company/about.html`; the image disappears.
walkthrough: From /company/, the same URL now resolves to /company/img/team.jpg — which doesn't exist.
Fix: use the root-relative `/img/team.jpg`, or update it to `../img/team.jpg`.
examples.result: The image loads again from its real location.

misconceptions.mistakenBelief: Relative URLs always resolve from the website root.
misconceptions.correction: Relative URLs resolve from the current document's location (its base); only URLs starting with / resolve from the site root. The same relative href can point to different places on different pages.
misconceptions.diagnosticPrompt: In "The link that broke after moving a page", why did the same href break?

analogy.example: Relative URLs are like **directions from where you're standing**: "go back one street, then turn into Css Lane". Root-relative is "from the town square"; absolute is a full postal address.
usefulFor: remembering relative depends on your position
choosing the right kind of address
limitations: Streets don't have index.html; folders do.
Fragments are like "room 12 in this building".

steps.explanation: The relative link resolves from the current page's folder.
The .. segment moves up one folder.
The css/ segment enters the folder, so the link resolves to /courses/css/.

trace.textAlternative: Resolving a relative course link. Step 1, Current base: folder is /courses/html/. The relative link resolves from the current page's folder. Step 2, Go up: after .. is /courses/. The .. segment moves up one folder. Step 3, Enter css: result is /courses/css/. The css/ segment enters the folder, so the link resolves to /courses/css/.

remediation.explanation: To debug a link: write the current page's folder, apply each segment of the href (`..` = up, name = into), and compare the result with where the file really is.
remediation.retryPrompt: Debug "The link that broke after moving a page" this way.

recap.summary: To construct and debug links across a multi-folder site, resolve relative URLs from the current page's folder, use / for root-relative, full URLs for other sites, and #id fragments for spots within a page that match an id exactly.
retrievalPrompts: Where does a relative URL resolve from?
Why might a #fragment link do nothing?
